title: Identity-point composition normalization at all coefficient stages
statement:
Fix a six-functor datum [def-sf-datum], with $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$, $\ell\ne\operatorname{char}k$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, its valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$ and uniformizer $\varpi_E$, and $n\geq1$. Put $A_{E,n}=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n$ and choose $\Lambda\in\{A_{E,n},\mathcal O_E,E,\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell\}$. Let $X$ be a separated finite-type $k$-scheme, $s=\operatorname{Spec}k$, and $a:X\to s$ its structure morphism. Use the datum's constructible finite-Tor categories and exceptional adjunctions; at the integral stage use the specified completed operations with compatible etale-origin witnesses on finite reductions, at $E$ their raw scalar localization, and at $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$ their common finite coefficient stages, on the corresponding domains of [fix-lem-exchanges]. Write $I=R\mathrm{id}_{s!}$ and $J=R\mathrm{id}_s^!$. Let $\alpha_{\mathrm{id}_s,a}:IRa_!\xrightarrow{\sim}Ra_!$ be the specified compact-support composition comparison: at finite coefficients the comparison of [thm-sf-comp-composition], integrally the specified completed comparison of [fix-lem-exchanges](2),(4), and at field coefficients its scalar-localized or common-stage image as in the same node. Let $v:I\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathrm{id}$ be the canonical identity comparison: finite-level identity compactification, integrally the inverse of the actual reduction/total-limit unit $u_C:C\to\mathcal L_s\mathcal R_sC$ of [lem-coef-derived-system-evaluation-calculus], and at field coefficients its scalar image. Then $\alpha_{\mathrm{id}_s,a}=vRa_!$; equivalently it is the identity under this comparison at every listed coefficient stage.

Let $e:IJ\to\mathrm{id}$ be the counit of $I\dashv J$, put $\omega_s=J\Lambda_s$, and define the identity-normalized counit
$$\nu=e_{\Lambda_s}\circ v_{J\Lambda_s}^{-1}:\omega_s\longrightarrow\Lambda_s.$$
Let $c:Ra^!\omega_s\to Ra^!\Lambda_s$ be the inverse of the right-adjoint mate of $\alpha_{\mathrm{id}_s,a}$; equivalently it is the conjugate of $\alpha_{\mathrm{id}_s,a}^{-1}$ with respect to $Ra_!\dashv Ra^!$ and the composite adjunction $IRa_!\dashv Ra^!J$, with pasted unit and counit. Then $\nu$ and $c$ are isomorphisms, $c=Ra^!(\nu)$, and, for the counit $\varepsilon^!_N:Ra_!Ra^!N\to N$,
$$\varepsilon^!_{\Lambda_s}\circ Ra_!(c)=\nu\circ\varepsilon^!_{\omega_s}.$$
These are equations of morphisms in the actual coefficient category at the chosen stage; the integral assertion concerns the specified completed composition comparison itself.

proof.text: Apply the finite identity-composition normalization to the finite operation datum and the higher identity-composition normalization to obtain the completed, rational, common-stage and finite-subfield identity isomorphisms, their left-adjoint normalization laws, and the specified coefficient squares.

For any stage write F ⊣ G and I ⊣ J. Conjugating v inverse from the identity adjunction gives the natural isomorphism w:J ≅ id with component v inverse at J L followed by the I ⊣ J counit. Thus the normalized counit is invertible. This is identity_stage_laws in Lean, using conjugateEquiv_adjunction_id.

The normalization alpha_K=v_(F K) implies alpha inverse_K=v inverse_(F K) by cancellation. Expand the mate of alpha inverse with the pasted adjunction counit. Naturality of v inverse at the F ⊣ G counit moves it to J L; the G triangle identity cancels the unit and counit. The result is c_L=G(v inverse_(J L) e_L)=G(nu_L), exactly identity_mate_formula.

A component of the mate isomorphism is invertible. Substitute c_L=G(nu_L) in naturality of the exceptional counit to obtain the required morphism equation. Package these statements with the normalization law on the required predicate, at each of the six displayed kinds of coefficient stage, retaining every coefficient square from the first step.

proof_origin.place: Steps 1--4 are isolated as two left-adjoint normalization lemmas; steps 5--7 are proved directly using Mathlib conjugation and adjunction identities.

split_report.summary: Repairs the returned C3/C4/E5 gap by introducing a general comparison lemma between the constant-tower word normalization of completed compact-support composition and the explicit semilinear reduction/total-limit counit formula. Steps 2–3 cite that formula from the new statement, including the identity compactification d=1, rather than from the proof of the realization lemma. Restores fix-lem-exchanges(2),(4) as the comparison named in the statement and used by the parents. The actual unit/counit triangle then proves identity normalization; Steps 1 and 4–7 are retained. One statement-only new node, no Mathlib leaves.
split_report.blueprint: The pairing-identification proof identifies the trace as the exceptional-adjunction counit. These steps supply its identity-point normalization; that calculation is agent-written and not claimed to appear in the blueprint.

tool_uses.why: Finite compact-support identity normalization is used as a generic composition tool; the identification unit has no construction of finite compact-support composition.
Its actual strict-tower, localized and common-stage compact-support functors fix the concrete objects and maps being normalized.
Its actual reduction/total-limit adjunction, unit, counit and triangle identities are needed for the completed identity calculation.
Its identity-open specialization fixes the inverse actual completion unit and proves its invertibility on derived-complete inputs.
The statement assumes this datum; its A1 and A5 provide precisely the adjunction and coefficient-compatibility structure used.
Its unital system compositors and identity proper/open maps compute the identity compactification before realization.
Its explicit localized Hom groups allow the equation and naturality to be checked on fractions.
Its common-stage morphism classes allow equality to be checked at the chosen finite coefficient field.
Its component formula and invertibility assertion compute the right identity comparison and composite mate.
Its identity adjunction and pasted counit formula type the conjugation calculations.
Only its stated normalized/common-bound system domains are used in Step 2. No normalization is inferred from its unspecified family c_V.

Its clauses (2),(4) specify the completed and transported composition comparison already used by the parent and sibling. The new bridge compares that same constant-tower word construction to the actual semilinear counit formula.
